note: The visual site-characterisation form, modelled on the OneAquaHealth field sampling protocol's site sheet (geolocation, water and habitat description, hydromorphology, land cover) and cut down to what a citizen with a phone can honestly judge. This file is the single source of truth: the vision model's output schema, the server-side validation, the questions the guided workflow asks, and the pressure scoring are all generated from it, so adding an indicator is one edit here. score runs 0 (no pressure) to 3 (severe); weight is how much the indicator moves the overall pressure number. photo_visible marks indicators a model can judge from an image at all - the rest can only come from a person standing in the stream, which is why the workflow asks.

indicators.question: How clear is the water?
indicators.why: Suspended sediment smothers the gravel that insect larvae and fish eggs need, and carries phosphorus and bacteria with it.

options.label: Clear - I can see the bed
Cloudy - the bed disappears in shallow water
Opaque - I cannot see in at all

indicators.question: What colour is the water?
indicators.why: Colour points at the source: green means algae, grey or black means sewage or sludge, orange means iron or mine drainage.

options.label: Natural - clear, or tea-coloured from peat or leaves
Grey or milky
options.note: possible sewage, concrete washings or industrial discharge

options.label: Orange or rust-red
options.note: iron, or drainage from made ground

options.label: An unusual colour I cannot place

indicators.question: How much algae is there?
indicators.why: Thick algae is the visible face of nutrient pollution. It swings oxygen wildly between day and night and some blooms are toxic to dogs, livestock and people.

options.label: None or a thin film on stones
Extensive - long strands or most stones covered
Mats, scum or a blue-green paint-like bloom
options.note: possible cyanobacteria; do not let dogs or children in

indicators.question: Is there foam or an oily film?
indicators.why: Natural foam is tan and breaks up; persistent white foam suggests detergent, and a rainbow sheen suggests oil from a road drain.

options.label: Tan-coloured foam below a fall, which breaks up
options.note: natural - dissolved plant matter whipped by turbulence

options.label: Persistent white or soapy foam
options.note: possible detergent or a misconnected drain

options.label: Rainbow film on the surface
options.note: possible oil or fuel from surface-water drainage

indicators.question: How much litter can you see?
indicators.why: Litter is the pressure citizens notice first and the one a community can fix itself. It also traps sediment and releases plastics.

options.label: A lot, or trapped in rafts
Wet wipes, sanitary items or toilet paper on the banks
options.note: a direct sign of sewage overflow - report this

indicators.question: What is growing along the banks?
indicators.why: A vegetated buffer shades the water, holds the bank together and filters run-off before it arrives. Mown grass to the edge does almost none of that.

options.label: Continuous trees, shrubs or tall plants
Mown grass right to the water

indicators.question: What are the banks made of?
indicators.why: Hydromorphology is the pressure European urban streams fail on most often. A concrete channel moves water fast and gives nothing anywhere to live.

options.label: Partly reinforced - some walls, gabions or rip-rap

indicators.question: How is the water moving?
indicators.why: Moving water carries oxygen. Standing warm water loses it, and still water is where mosquitoes breed.

options.label: Fast, broken and splashing over stones
Standing pools, no flow
options.note: low oxygen and mosquito breeding habitat

options.label: Dry bed
options.note: record it - drying is a climate and abstraction signal

indicators.question: What is the stream bed made of?
indicators.why: Insect larvae need the gaps between stones. Silt or concrete fills or removes them, so the sensitive animals have nowhere to live even if the water is clean.

indicators.question: Is there sludge or heavy silt on the bed?
indicators.why: A black, smelly layer means the sediment has run out of oxygen. Nothing sensitive lives in it.

options.label: Thick silt, or black sludge that smells when disturbed

indicators.question: How shaded is the water?
indicators.why: Shade keeps the water cool as the climate warms. Cold water holds more oxygen and is what sensitive species need.

indicators.question: What can you smell? (only you can answer this)
indicators.why: Smell separates a cloudy but healthy stream in spate from a sewage discharge, and no camera can report it. This is the field where the person, not the model, decides.

options.label: Sewage or rotten eggs
options.note: report this to the water authority today

options.label: Chemical, solvent or fuel
options.note: do not enter the water; report it

indicators.question: Do people or animals use this water?
indicators.why: The One Health question. A degraded stream nobody touches is an ecological problem; a degraded stream children paddle in is also a public-health one.

options.label: People or dogs get into the water
Children play in it, or animals drink from it
